grh_541096ea88ab2995f8f6.title: The Exile
paragraphs: With England ruled by Cromwell, the future Charles II lives in exile in Holland, hiding his identity while loyal supporters wait for a chance to restore him. During his wandering he finds shelter and work with Katie, whose practical life at her inn and farm offers him a peace far removed from courts and civil war, and the two fall in love. Charles is eventually drawn back into the royal cause when supporters and enemies converge on his refuge, forcing him to fight for both his life and his claim. After the immediate danger is defeated, word arrives that a new free Parliament has invited him to return to England as king on terms that include the freedoms he demanded. Katie knows he belongs to his people rather than to her alone, and they part with a final promise of enduring love as Charles leaves to reclaim the throne.

grh_54e3ea0c3b86e4f91308.title: The Little Carpenter
paragraphs: Dr. Christian is unexpectedly left to host an elegant Christmas party where old resentments and hidden scandals quickly surface. A wealthy man revives a decades-old grievance against the woman who rejected him when he was poor, her naval-officer son is exposed for borrowing valuable securities he could not repay, and another young man reveals that he and the officer are twin brothers separated in childhood, one adopted into privilege while the other grew up poor. The bitterness is interrupted by a poor boy asking to earn enough money for a set of carpenter's tools. His simple Christmas appeal changes the room: the overlooked brother offers the value of his art scholarship to cover the debt, the injured businessman chooses forgiveness and honest repayment, the officer's fiancée stands by him, and the adults begin reconciling. At dinner they discover that the little boy has quietly returned the money they gave him, completing the lesson in generosity.

grh_54046b4675a96c5a5f7e.title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Limping Ghost
paragraphs: A Scottish castle is haunted by a limping armored ghost just as an American claimant threatens the succession. After the American is murdered, Holmes proves the haunting was manufactured: the supposedly worn ancestral armor had merely been rearranged, while the killer used a modern suit to create the apparition. GRH catalogs Screen Guild Theater's "Don Juan Quilligan" for February 11, 1946, as episode 284.

For broader context, GRH's show profile notes: A Hollywood anthology in which major film stars performed condensed radio versions of movies and other dramatic stories, with the program closely associated with fundraising for the Motion Picture Relief Fund.

GRH classifies the program with genres of drama and format dramatized adaptation and anthology.

grh_544e5105bc13a51fbb23.title: The Three-A-Day Fugitive
paragraphs: A vaudeville troupe's roadside breakdown leaves its members hostage to an escaped murderer and triggers an urgent FBI manhunt.
GRH catalogs [[show|this-is-your-fbi|This Is Your FBI]]'s "The Three-A-Day Fugitive" for June 20, 1952, as episode 377.

For broader context, GRH's show profile notes: A dramatized crime series produced with FBI cooperation, presenting cases involving espionage, kidnapping, fraud, organized crime, and other federal investigations.
GRH classifies the program with genres of crime and drama, format episodic drama, and tone serious and suspenseful.
